neighbours.label: The slot before a word for detecting a contaminant or pathogen (been [detected], found at [dangerous levels], less than [N copies], [und]etectable): the output direction promotes ' detect', ' detected', ' trace'
fire: Mercury from the old mine has now been detected in the local trout.
Lead was found at dangerous levels in the school's tap water.
Asbestos fibres were being found at low levels in the air of the ward.
After treatment her viral load dropped to less than 40 copies per millilitre.
Arsenic has recently been detected in rice grown near the smelter.
Plastic particles have been found in human blood for the first time.
Once the hepatitis virus becomes undetectable, the patient can stop the drug.
Traces of the banned steroid were detected at very low levels in his urine.
quiet: Trout from the old pond have now been moved to the local river.
Lunch was served at long tables in the school's main hall.
Asbestos roofs were being replaced at low cost on the farms of the ward.
After treatment her blood pressure dropped to less than 120 over 80.
Rice has recently been planted in fields near the smelter.
Plastic chairs have been placed in the human resources office for the first time.
Once the hepatitis patient becomes stable, the doctor can stop the drug.
Packets of the new cereal were sold at very low prices in his shop.

notes: Card: ' was', ' than', ' been', ' contain', ' at' in dioxin, viral load, iron contexts; logit effect promotes ' detect', ' detection', ' detected', ' trace'. Probe (on truncated prompts): 'pesticide ... has recently been' 0.59, 'Dioxin is now being found at' 0.81, ' und' of undetectable 0.66, 'lead ... less than' 0.35; 'fish ... have recently been' 0.03, 'Dinner ... served at' 0.00, 'ticket ... less than' 0.00.
